subject.title: [Feature]: Native E2EE Browser Chat, No Third-Party Required

question: Should OpenClaw pursue native no-third-party browser-held E2EE chat in core, define plugin/Gateway seams for an external transport first, or decline this direction in favor of existing WebChat plus channel plugins?
rationale: The current code does not implement the requested capability, and the right owner boundary plus security model cannot be chosen safely by cleanup automation.

options.title: Design core E2EE browser chat
options.body: Sponsor a core architecture effort covering keys, encrypted envelopes, pairing, storage, relay fallback, and UI before accepting implementation PRs.

options.title: Define plugin/Gateway seams first
options.body: Keep core lean by specifying the missing protocol and plugin APIs that would let a ClawHub/browser-chat plugin integrate safely.

options.title: Decline native transport
options.body: Close the direction after documenting that WebChat, Tailscale/SSH, and channel plugins are the supported no-new-core path.

recommendation.title: Design core E2EE browser chat
recommendation.body: Sponsor a core architecture effort covering keys, encrypted envelopes, pairing, storage, relay fallback, and UI before accepting implementation PRs.
